engineering.question: I've never written code before. Will I struggle in first year?

answer.text: I hadn't coded before either. What helped most was practising a little every day and asking for help early instead of waiting until exams.

engineering.question: How do I get involved in projects outside class?

answer.text: Join one student team or club in your first semester and stay with it for a year. You learn more from building something with people than from collecting certificates.

medicine.question: How do you keep up with the amount of reading?

answer.text: Plan the week on Sunday and revise a little every day. Cramming doesn't work at this volume — small daily reviews do.

medicine.question: When do you start seeing patients?

dental.question: Is the practical work hard to get used to?

answer.text: It felt slow at first. Practising the same steps again and again is normal — everyone in my batch improved a lot by the second year.

dental.question: How much time do you get for yourself?

default.question: What should I do in the summer before joining?

answer.text: Rest, and read about your subject for fun. You don't need to prepare everything in advance — the first weeks are for settling in.

default.question: Is it easy to make friends in the first week?

answer.text: Say yes to the first few events, even the awkward ones. Most people are as new as you are.
